title: The Broken Light That Saved Him
surface: A man deliberately damages the taillight of a moving car. Police stop it, let him out and take the driver away. He is neither a mechanic nor an officer and has no permission from the owner. Why is he rescued instead of being immediately taken away?
solution: He is a kidnapping victim trapped in the trunk; the driver is his captor. Damaging the taillight from inside is an attempt to draw attention. A patrol stops the car over the faulty light, discovers the trapped victim and frees him, then detains the driver.

facts.text: The man is a kidnapping victim locked in the trunk, and the driver is his captor.
The damaged light prompts a stop that reveals the victim and leads to his rescue.
The story concerns the immediate rescue, not later compensation or a court verdict.

unknowns: The motive, car model and exact method of damaging the light are unspecified.
hints: What does “let him out” imply about his original position?
He can reach a rear light without being outside the car.
He is trapped in the trunk and trying to attract help.
